A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sequential-NIAH benchmark and evaluation model. Their text, figures, tables and equations are readable and matchable across the revision. V3's appendices are fully available; v1 ends with references.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluator results on 1,960 synthetic examples, benchmark results for six LLMs on 2,000 samples, and positional/order noise experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds Qwen-3 results, model-size experiments, semantic-noise results and failure-mode analyses.

M1.justification: The three needle-generation pipelines, shuffle-and-insert construction algorithm, synthetic evaluator-training procedure and Qwen2.5-32B evaluator remain the same. Pipeline renaming and newly supplied prompts and checking details do not establish a changed underlying method.

E1.justification: The Chinese/English benchmark, ICEWS/FEG, private QA source and LongData-Corpus coverage remain unchanged. V3 adds a semantic-distractor scenario with one or two misleading, answer-invalid needles in the context (Section 5.3). The renamed generation pipelines do not represent new datasets.

E2.justification: V3 adds Qwen3-32B to the main comparison and evaluates Qwen2.5-32B/7B and Qwen3-14B/8B in scaling and failure analyses. The original six main models, Claude-3.5/GPT-4o evaluator comparators, and three noise-analysis models are retained.

E3.justification: V3 introduces model-size comparisons and extends the existing 200-sample noise design from three perturbation types and 1,800 perturbed samples to four types and 2,400. Three variants per type remain. Benchmark splits, original accuracy-based evaluations and evaluator-training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands diagnostics through model-size sensitivity (Figure 5), semantic-distractor robustness (Table 5), detailed evaluator breakdowns (Table 7), and failure-mode analysis (Table 8). The earlier grouped noise-consistency analysis is retained and relocated from v1 Figure 6 to v3 Appendix D/Figure 7.

E5.justification: V3 Table 5 introduces ± values for noise-group and pooled accuracies, whereas v1 reports means alone. V3 does not define what these quantities represent or establish additional repeated runs. Three perturbation variants per noise type were already reported in v1.

E6.justification: Figure 4 revises retained-model scores, including Gemini-1.5 from 63.15% to 63.50% and Qwen-2.5 from 51.10% to 50.05%, and adds Qwen3-32B at 44.70%. Scaling results, semantic-noise outcomes, evaluator breakdowns and failure counts are newly reported. Table 5's pooled results now include semantic noise, so their changes are not same-condition performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the conditional-likelihood objective in Equation 1 retain their mathematical content. Renaming algorithm outputs to Query and Answer is not a theoretical revision. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The benchmark, trained evaluator and challenging sequential-retrieval task remain the main contributions. V3 adds explicit claims that its evaluator is more efficient and cheaper than GPT-4o and Claude; v1 describes it as reliable and efficient without that comparative cost claim.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets Qwen's fewer irrelevant or additional-content errors as suggesting stronger question understanding. The noise discussion now treats pooled accuracy deviations below 6% as acceptable and revises its explanation of response stability. The stated domain-bias and API-setting limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices F–G newly disclose generation and evaluator prompts, implementation snippets, 8-H20-GPU deployment, approximately 97 million inference tokens, and timing estimates. V3 also documents manual QA sampling checks and replaces the anonymous repository link with named GitHub access information. These additions substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to the retained procedure.

R1.justification: V3 adds FactGuard (Zhang et al., 2025) to the long-context benchmark discussion and references. The existing positioning relative to NIAH benchmarks, long-context models and evaluation methods is largely retained.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites and condenses the introduction, construction explanation, experimental discussion and conclusion. It standardizes temporal/logical pipeline terminology and reorganizes material into appendices, including the existing grouped noise discussion. These changes extend well beyond local copyediting.

P2.justification: V3 replaces the ACM-style formatting and author block, redraws Figure 2, adds scaling, noise-example and prompt figures, and introduces Tables 6–8. Table 5 gains a semantic-noise column and uncertainty rows. The original grouped noise figure moves to the appendix as Figure 7.

improvement.justification: V3 improves reproducibility through explicit prompts and resource disclosures, and its scaling, semantic-noise and failure analyses make the benchmark more informative. Reporting problems limit the gain: revised main scores are unexplained, Table 5's ± values are undefined, and Appendix D reuses the earlier grouped-noise results while referring to all noise groups. The net improvement is positive but qualified.
